scope.statement: This artifact records theory-linked, falsifiable predictions and analysis boundaries. It neither diagnoses consciousness in any person or system nor authorizes data collection.

sources.title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
limitations: The tests operationalize selected biological predictions rather than every formulation of either theory.
Results across fMRI, MEG, and intracranial EEG depend on different spatial and temporal sensitivities.

sources.title: Integrated information theory (IIT) 4.0: Formulating the properties of phenomenal existence in physical terms
limitations: The formal postulates do not uniquely determine the non-invasive neural proxies used here.
Feasible experiments can test consequences of an implementation without computing full intrinsic cause-effect structure.

sources.title: Conscious Processing and the Global Neuronal Workspace Hypothesis
limitations: The review synthesizes heterogeneous paradigms rather than preregistering the present contrasts.
Putative ignition and broadcasting measures are sensitive to task and report requirements.

sources.title: Towards a true neural stance on consciousness
limitations: The proposed role of local recurrence does not supply a unique measurement or perturbation protocol.
Later work disputes whether recurrence is necessary or sufficient for conscious experience.

sources.title: Is recurrent processing necessary and/or sufficient for consciousness?
limitations: The article is a conceptual critique rather than a decisive causal experiment.
Attention, recurrence, and report remain difficult to manipulate independently.

sources.title: Empirical support for higher-order theories of conscious awareness
limitations: Metacognitive measures can reflect decision noise, memory, or response strategy rather than higher-order representation.
The theory family permits multiple neural implementations.

sources.title: An embarrassment of richnesses: the PFC isn’t the content NCC
limitations: The analysis constrains localization claims but does not adjudicate all higher-order accounts.
Anatomical dissociations do not alone identify the representational level of a signal.

sources.title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
limitations: Theory-derived indicators are not validated diagnostic tests for artificial consciousness.
Behavioral or architectural resemblance can arise without the hypothesized causal organization.

requiredBeforeExecution: institutional ethics approval and informed consent
registrationGate.humanRole: Humans serve only where legal consent or institutional ethics approval cannot be automated; automated review, preregistration preparation, and analysis validation remain the operating body.

blinding.mappingCustodian: An automated, access-separated preregistration custodian generates a hash-pinned analyst package containing only blinded labels, measurements, criteria, and controls; analysts must not have repository or mapping access until unblinding.
blinding.unblindingTrigger: The custodian releases the separately sealed label-to-theory mapping only after exclusions, model code, confirmatory outputs, and the signed analysis-complete manifest are locked.
blinding.executionRequirement: Before recruitment, independent review must verify access separation, reproduce the analyst-package hash, and dry-run the one-way unblinding trigger.

theoryFamilies.name: Integrated Information Theory
limitations: The registered measurements test selected biological implementation claims, not the complete mathematical theory.
A failed neural proxy does not establish that every possible IIT implementation is false.

theoryFamilies.name: Global Neuronal Workspace Theory
limitations: Task, report, and post-perceptual activity can mimic workspace signatures.
The registered tests distinguish specified neural implementations from the broader computational idea of global availability.

theoryFamilies.name: Recurrent Processing Theory
limitations: Recurrence is widespread and its observation alone may not distinguish conscious processing from attention or inference.
Causal perturbation can disrupt feedforward evidence or task performance as well as the targeted recurrent computation.

theoryFamilies.name: Higher-Order Theory
limitations: Confidence and metacognitive accuracy are imperfect operational proxies for higher-order representation.
Higher-order theories do not uniformly require prefrontal cortex, so localization cannot stand in for the whole family.

predictions.title: Location and dimensionality of maintained conscious content

measurement.population: Consenting adults with normal or corrected vision; any clinical intracranial cohort is analyzed separately.
measurement.design: Within-subject factorial presentation of faces, objects, symbols, and orientations with task relevance counterbalanced and stimulus identity decoded on a held-out test set.
primaryVariables: cross-validated category decoding by preregistered region
analysisPlan: Freeze posterior-cortical and prefrontal regions before unblinding theory labels.
Train decoders only on the optimization split and report locked accuracy with hierarchical participant effects on the test split.
Control family-wise error across regions, content dimensions, and time windows using the preregistered permutation maximum statistic.
measurement.sampleSizeJustification: Determine sample size by simulation before recruitment, targeting 90% power for the smallest preregistered cross-validated decoding contrast while preserving a held-out confirmatory set.

criteria.pass: A theory-linked region carries both preregistered content dimensions above the locked permutation threshold throughout the maintenance window.
criteria.fail: Neither content dimension exceeds the locked threshold in the theory-linked region despite positive sensory and behavioral controls.
criteria.inconclusive: Only one dimension passes, reliability is below the preregistered floor, or positive controls fail.
criteria.thresholdPolicy: Regions, windows, minimum reliability, and corrected alpha are preregistered before confirmatory data access.

confounders.control: Counterbalance task relevance and separate stimulus-period decoding from response-period activity.
Use participant-level functional localizers, noise ceilings, and matched positive-control decoding.

interpretations.expectedResult: Maximal multidimensional content information is sustained in posterior cortex.
interpretations.consequence: Posterior maintenance supports the tested IIT biological implementation; its absence challenges that implementation.

interpretations.expectedResult: Conscious content is decodable in prefrontal workspace regions as part of global availability.
interpretations.consequence: Prefrontal content coding supports the tested GNWT implementation; its absence under adequate sensitivity challenges that implementation.

neutrality.forbiddenInference: Passing or failing this contrast cannot establish the presence or absence of consciousness or the truth or falsity of an entire theory family.

measurement.population: The same consenting adult and separately analyzed clinical cohorts as CPR-A.
measurement.design: Variable-duration visible stimuli followed by a delayed response, with duration jitter separating onset, maintenance, offset, and report epochs.
primaryVariables: posterior sustained amplitude and representational stability
analysisPlan: Estimate preregistered onset, middle-duration, and offset windows without using response-period samples.
Test duration scaling and temporal generalization on held-out trials.
Require cross-modal directional agreement while reporting modality-specific estimates.
measurement.sampleSizeJustification: Use simulation from optimization data to achieve 90% power for both duration scaling and onset/offset contrasts under the corrected sequential decision rule.

criteria.pass: The preregistered sustained or onset-offset signature exceeds its corrected threshold and replicates directionally across two modalities.
criteria.fail: The signature remains below threshold with adequate noise ceiling and successful sensory controls in both modalities.
criteria.inconclusive: Modalities disagree, duration manipulation fails, or the estimate falls inside the smallest-effect-of-interest interval.
criteria.thresholdPolicy: Windows, smallest effects of interest, replication rule, and multiplicity correction are fixed before confirmatory data access.

confounders.confounder: Stimulus transients mistaken for theory signatures
confounders.control: Jitter duration and model onset, maintenance, and offset separately.
Exclude response epochs and include matched delayed-response catch trials.

interpretations.expectedResult: Posterior content-specific activity and interactions persist for the experienced duration.
interpretations.consequence: Sustained posterior evidence supports the specified IIT implementation; absent maintenance challenges it.

interpretations.expectedResult: Brief prefrontal ignition occurs near onset and offset with relatively silent intervening maintenance.
interpretations.consequence: The double-ignition profile supports the specified GNWT implementation; absent offset ignition challenges it.

neutrality.forbiddenInference: Temporal signatures alone cannot prove consciousness or conclusively validate or invalidate a whole theory.

predictions.title: Short-range posterior versus long-range workspace interaction

measurement.population: Consenting adults; intracranial coverage is treated as a separate opportunistic replication stratum.
measurement.design: Within-subject visible-content trials with prestimulus baselines, task relevance counterbalancing, and directionally specified connectivity edges.
analysisPlan: Lock nodes, directions, frequency bands, and windows on optimization data.
Compare content-present trials with signal- and task-matched controls using leakage-resistant estimators.
Confirm topology with a preregistered multilevel contrast rather than selecting the strongest edges post hoc.
measurement.sampleSizeJustification: Run simulation with empirically estimated edge covariance to obtain 90% power for the preregistered topology contrast after correction.

criteria.pass: The predicted topology contrast exceeds the corrected threshold during the locked maintenance window and generalizes to held-out participants.
criteria.fail: The predicted topology is absent or directionally reversed despite adequate node reliability and positive controls.
criteria.inconclusive: Motion, leakage, coverage, or node reliability violates the preregistered quality floor.
criteria.thresholdPolicy: All nodes, edges, directions, bands, quality floors, and corrected thresholds are preregistered before test-set access.

confounders.control: Use leakage-resistant connectivity metrics and simulated null networks.
Condition on early sensory responses and compare directed lagged interactions.

interpretations.expectedResult: Sustained short-range posterior interactions dominate the specified contrast.
interpretations.consequence: That topology supports the tested posterior IIT implementation; its reliable absence challenges it.

interpretations.expectedResult: Long-range interactions between high-level content regions and prefrontal workspace dominate.
interpretations.consequence: That topology supports the tested GNWT implementation; its reliable absence challenges it.

neutrality.forbiddenInference: A connectivity topology is not by itself evidence that consciousness exists or that a complete theory is true.

predictions.title: Causal necessity of early visual recurrent processing

measurement.population: Consenting adults screened for non-invasive stimulation contraindications.
measurement.design: Randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled perturbation at individually localized feedforward and recurrent windows during threshold visual perception.
analysisPlan: Estimate participant-specific timing using an independent localizer.
Test the stimulation-window by condition interaction with hierarchical models and equivalence bounds for feedforward performance.
Exclude trials with preregistered blink, muscle, or auditory-evoked contamination.
measurement.sampleSizeJustification: Use blinded pilot variance in a simulation-based power analysis for the interaction and equivalence tests, targeting 90% power with attrition reserve.

criteria.pass: Recurrent-window perturbation selectively reduces visibility and the recurrent component while feedforward sensitivity remains within the equivalence bound.
criteria.fail: Recurrent-window perturbation is equivalent to sham for visibility despite verified target engagement and adequate precision.
criteria.inconclusive: Target engagement fails, feedforward sensitivity is also impaired, or confidence intervals cross both the effect and equivalence bounds.
criteria.thresholdPolicy: Timing, target-engagement floor, effect threshold, equivalence bounds, exclusions, and alpha are preregistered before outcome unblinding.

confounders.control: Use matched sham, masking noise, participant blinding checks, and sensory covariates.

confounders.confounder: Disrupted feedforward encoding rather than recurrence
confounders.control: Independently localize timing and require preserved type-1 sensitivity within a preregistered equivalence bound.

interpretations.expectedResult: Selective perturbation of recurrent processing reduces visual awareness despite preserved feedforward encoding.
interpretations.consequence: Selective impairment supports recurrence necessity in the tested task; a precise null with target engagement challenges that claim.

interpretations.expectedResult: Local recurrent disruption affects conscious report only when it prevents later global availability.
interpretations.consequence: Mediation by later workspace measures favors a global-availability account over recurrence alone.

neutrality.forbiddenInference: A causal effect on report cannot alone establish consciousness or show that recurrence is sufficient or an entire rival theory is false.

predictions.title: Higher-order metacognitive representation dissociated from first-order performance

measurement.population: Consenting adults performing calibrated near-threshold visual discrimination.
measurement.design: Within-subject manipulation of metacognitive access while staircase procedures equate first-order sensitivity and response bias across conditions.
measurement.manipulation: After the initial forced-choice response, randomly present informative, uninformative, or direction-reversed post-decision evidence before the confidence response; evidence strength is adaptively calibrated on separate trials and never changes the already-recorded first-order choice.
analysisPlan: Fit hierarchical signal-detection models with blinded condition labels.
Require first-order sensitivity and bias equivalence before interpreting metacognitive contrasts.
Validate manipulation-strength using the preregistered monotonic confidence-calibration contrast across informative, uninformative, and reversed post-decision evidence.
Test representational mediation without presuming that higher-order signals are prefrontal.
measurement.sampleSizeJustification: Select sample size using simulation of the hierarchical meta-d-prime model for 90% power and adequate precision on both the dissociation and equivalence tests.

criteria.pass: Metacognitive efficiency and a cross-validated higher-order signal change while first-order sensitivity and bias remain equivalent.
criteria.fail: Metacognitive measures are equivalent across conditions with adequate precision and validated manipulation strength.
criteria.inconclusive: First-order equivalence fails, model recovery is inadequate, or neural results depend on an unregistered region choice.
criteria.thresholdPolicy: Equivalence margins, model-recovery criteria, regions or searchlight correction, and mediation tests are preregistered before unblinding.

confounders.control: Use adaptive staircases and require preregistered d-prime and bias equivalence.

confounders.confounder: Confidence scale and motor response artifacts
confounders.control: Counterbalance mappings, model scale use, and separate confidence timing from perceptual response.

interpretations.expectedResult: Awareness-linked metacognitive change occurs independently of matched first-order discrimination.
interpretations.consequence: A robust dissociation supports a higher-order representation account; a precise null challenges the tested operationalization.

interpretations.expectedResult: First-order recurrent sensory processing can support perceptual awareness without a necessary metacognitive-efficiency change.
interpretations.consequence: Preserved perceptual report under reduced metacognition is compatible with separating local recurrence from higher-order access.

neutrality.forbiddenInference: Metacognitive efficiency is not a direct meter of consciousness, and localization cannot validate or falsify every higher-order theory.

predictions.title: Content signatures invariant to task relevance and immediate report

measurement.population: Consenting adults completing report, delayed-report, and task-irrelevant viewing conditions.
measurement.design: Within-subject factorial manipulation of stimulus visibility, task relevance, and report timing with occasional orthogonal probes validating perception.
analysisPlan: Train content decoders in one report condition and test generalization in the others.
Separate report-locked and stimulus-locked components with temporal generalization and nuisance regressors.
Interpret only conditions meeting preregistered probe, fixation, arousal, and decoder-reliability floors.
measurement.sampleSizeJustification: Use simulation of the smallest cross-condition generalization effect and planned interaction to achieve 90% power after correction, with a precision stopping rule fixed before recruitment.

criteria.pass: A content signature generalizes above the corrected threshold across report and task-relevance conditions while report-linked activity dissociates.
criteria.fail: Content decoding does not generalize despite adequate within-condition reliability and validated perception probes.
criteria.inconclusive: Probe validity, arousal, fixation, or decoder reliability falls below its preregistered floor.
criteria.thresholdPolicy: Generalization contrasts, correction, reliability floors, and precision stopping are preregistered before confirmatory data access.

confounders.control: Use sparse orthogonal probes and model their carryover separately.
Match stimulus statistics, monitor eyes and pupils, and include preregistered arousal exclusions.

interpretations.expectedResult: Task-independent content remains globally available, while some late frontoparietal components vary with report demands.
interpretations.consequence: Cross-condition global content supports availability separated from motor report; report-only activity must not be counted as decisive ignition.

interpretations.expectedResult: Posterior recurrent content signatures persist when immediate report and task relevance are removed.
interpretations.consequence: Report-invariant posterior recurrence supports the tested local account; its absence with valid probes challenges it.

interpretations.expectedResult: Higher-order representation can generalize across response modes even if confidence-report activity does not.
interpretations.consequence: A report-invariant higher-order signal supports the tested operationalization, whereas a purely motor-linked signal does not.

neutrality.forbiddenInference: Report invariance does not itself demonstrate consciousness and cannot settle the truth of any entire theory family.
